# viewllm

**Browse and share HTML reports generated by AI coding agents.**

One command. Zero config. Works everywhere.

```bash
npx viewllm ./reports
```

## Why viewllm?

AI coding agents like **Claude Code**, **Codex**, and **Cursor** are increasingly generating rich, self-contained HTML reports — data visualizations, research analyses, comparison tables, interactive charts. HTML is becoming the new Markdown for AI output.

But viewing these reports is still painful:

- **VS Code Live Preview** breaks over SSH/WSL
- **GitHub** won't render HTML files
- **`python -m http.server`** gives you an ugly directory listing
- **Sharing** means downloading files and emailing them around

**viewllm** turns a folder of HTML files into a browsable, shareable report viewer — instantly.

## Features

- **Split-pane UI** — sidebar with file tree + full-width report viewer
- **Recently modified** — top N most recent files, always visible (configurable)
- **Unread tracking** — new/modified files marked with blue dots, per-device via localStorage
- **Live thumbnails** — miniature preview renders of each recent report
- **Text previews** — extracted text snippets for quick identification
- **Themes** — Light, Dark (Tokyo Night), and Solarized Light
- **Mobile-friendly** — responsive layout with pull-to-refresh
- **URL sharing** — hash-based links go directly to a specific report (`#path/to/file.html`)
- **Directory excludes** — auto-skips `venv/`, `node_modules/`, `.git/`, etc. (configurable)
- **Settings panel** — theme, preview toggles, recent count, exclude patterns — all per-device
- **Single binary** — no runtime dependencies, no build step, no framework
- **Auto-refresh** — polls for file changes every 2 seconds

## Quick Start

### npx (recommended — zero install)

```bash
npx viewllm ./path/to/html/reports
```

### Download binary

Grab the latest release for your platform from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/yz671/viewllm/releases):

```bash
# Linux (amd64)
curl -fsSL https://github.com/yz671/viewllm/releases/latest/download/viewllm-linux-amd64 -o viewllm
chmod +x viewllm
./viewllm ./reports
```

### Build from source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yz671/viewllm.git
cd viewllm
go build -o viewllm .
./viewllm ./reports
```

## Usage

```
viewllm <directory> [-p port] [-exclude dir]...
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `-p` | `8090` | Port to serve on |
| `-exclude` | — | Additional directories to ignore (repeatable) |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Serve on default port
viewllm ./reports

# Custom port
viewllm ./reports -p 8095

# Exclude additional directories
viewllm ./project -exclude logs -exclude tmp
```

## Use Cases

### AI coding agent reports
Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor generate HTML reports for code analysis, test results, and architecture reviews. Point viewllm at your project directory and browse them all.

```bash
viewllm ./my-project -p 8090
```

### Quant research
Share trading strategy comparisons, backtest results, and signal analysis reports with your team. Everyone gets their own unread tracking.

### Jupyter HTML exports
Export notebooks to HTML and serve them with a proper browse experience instead of raw file listings.

### Remote development
Working on a remote server via SSH or WSL? Start viewllm there and access it from your local browser. Pair with a tunnel for mobile access:

```bash
viewllm ./reports -p 8095 &
npx cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8095
```

## How It Works

viewllm is a single Go binary (~9MB) with the entire frontend embedded via `go:embed`. When you run it:

1. Scans the directory for `.html` files (skipping `venv/`, `node_modules/`, etc.)
2. Serves a split-pane web UI on the specified port
3. Polls the directory every 2 seconds for new/modified files
4. Frontend polls the API for updates and renders the sidebar + iframe viewer

There's no database, no config file, no build step. Stop the process and it's gone.

### API

```
GET /              → Web UI
GET /api/recent    → Recently modified HTML files (with text previews)
GET /api/tree      → Full directory tree as nested JSON
GET /api/excludes  → Current exclude patterns
GET /files/{path}  → Serves raw HTML file content
```

## Settings

Click the gear icon (top-right) to access per-device settings:

- **Theme** — Light, Dark, Solarized
- **Text preview** — show/hide text snippets in recent list
- **Thumbnail preview** — show/hide live mini-renders
- **Recent files count** — 0 (off), 3, 5, 10, 15, or 20
- **Ignored folders** — view built-in excludes, add/remove custom patterns

All settings are stored in your browser's localStorage — each device has its own preferences.

## Motivation

> "HTML is the new markdown. I've stopped writing markdown files for almost everything and switched to using Claude Code to generate HTML for me."
> — [Thariq Shihipar](https://x.com/trq212/status/2052811606032269638), Engineering Lead, Claude Code at Anthropic

The shift from Markdown to HTML for AI-generated reports is happening fast. Thariq's post hit 5M+ views and sparked widespread discussion — HTML gives AI a richer canvas for data visualizations, interactive tables, and research reports that Markdown simply can't express.

But generating HTML is only half the problem. You still need to **view** and **share** it. viewllm closes that gap — point it at a folder, get a beautiful browsable UI, share the link with your team.

## Tech Stack

- **Backend**: Go, stdlib only, zero external dependencies
- **Frontend**: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no framework, no build step
- **Embedding**: `go:embed` compiles the frontend into the binary
- **Architecture**: Polling-based file discovery, REST API, iframe-based report rendering

## Contributing

Contributions welcome! The codebase is intentionally simple:

```
viewllm/
  main.go              # Server, API handlers, file scanning
  frontend/
    index.html         # Entire UI (HTML + CSS + JS, embedded via go:embed)
  .github/
    workflows/
      release.yml      # Cross-platform binary builds
```
